card.text: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.

introduction.text: Mercury's cratered surface can reach 430 °C by day and drop to −180 °C at night.

normal.title: Low-Sun monochrome map
normal.summary: Images taken with the Sun low in the sky bring out crater rims and ridges.

color.title: MDIS 3-color mosaic
color.summary: Three filters, from violet light to near-infrared, show Mercury's subtle color differences, not the colors an eye would see.

enhanced.title: MDIS Enhanced Color Mosaic
enhanced.summary: Enhanced colors make subtle differences in Mercury’s surface easier to see.

topography.title: Height of craters and plains
topography.summary: Overlapping MESSENGER photographs reveal surface heights; colors show craters and plains above or below a reference sphere.

loi.title: Higher-Sun monochrome map
loi.summary: Images taken with the Sun higher in the sky show surface brightness patterns. The two maps use different brightness scales.

gravity.title: Gravity anomaly
gravity.summary: Radio tracking of MESSENGER measured where Mercury pulls a little harder or weaker. Detail is finer in the north.

crust.title: Crustal-thickness model
crust.summary: Thickness inferred from gravity and topography. It depends on assumed rock densities.
